newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W.Australia iron ore production seen rising.
newsitem.headline: W.Australia iron ore production seen rising.

text.p: Western Australia's iron ore industry will continue to grow before production stabilises by about 2005 at around 200 million tonnes a year, Western Australia's Resources Minister Colin Barnett said on Monday.
The state of Western Australia produced about 133.5 million tonnes (MT) of iron ore last year, almost all of which was exported.

In a statement issued with the release of the latest issue of the Western Australia Iron Ore Industry Review, Barnett said the expansion was likely to be fuelled by a number of factors including projected increases in demand.
"Japan has consistently maintained its position as the major buyer of Australian iron ore," Barnett said.
"However, increased sales to the rapidly growing economies of China, Korea and Taiwan have underpinned increased production," he said.
"The growth in export demand in Asia, combined with abundant reserves and cost advantages, should see the WA iron ore industry continue to expand."

The Industry Review, published by the Western Australian Department of Resources Development, said the International Iron and Steel Institute expected crude steel production to reach 776 million tonnes this year, compared with 751 million last year.
"Given the bullish outlook for world crude steel output, global iron ore production is expected to reach 1,031 MT in 1996 and 1,044 MT by 1997," the Review says.
Most of this production was expected to come from increased output from Western Australia, Brazil and South Africa.

"Iron ore production in Europe and the CIS is expected to fall. Western Australia and Brazil are expected to continue to dominate global iron ore trade, jointly accounting for approximately 60 percent of the market, which both countries have maintained since 1991," the review said.
It also forecast a bullish future for direct reduction iron/hot briquetted iron (DRI/HBI) in Western Australia.

It forecast the DRI market increasing by 29 million tonnes by the year 2005 with DRI/HBI as a percentage of electric arc furnace feed in east Asia going as high as 30 percent by this time, compared to an expected average global ratio of 16 percent
"Western Australia, with its abundance of low cost iron ore and competitively priced natural gas, appears to be well placed to supply DRI/HBI to this expanding east Asian market," the Review says.
"This includes a strategic geographical advantage over many other world locations in transport to Asian markets.
"WA exporters would have a freight cost differential of between $US10 per tonne and $US16 per tonne over the leading producer of DRI, Venezuela, if and whenn it wishes to sell into the Asian market.
"This is likely to more than compensate for the possibility of lower iron ore and gas prices in South America."
